title: habría = would have, me habría gustado, debería = should

cards.title: habría = would have
cards.body: Haber + -ía loses its e, like podría: habría (I / he / she / you formal would have).

cards.title: Long sentences, block by block
cards.body: Same structure as English. Venir is movement, so it takes a.

examples.en: We would have been able to go.
They would have been able to eat.
They would have come to eat.

cards.title: me habría gustado = I'd have liked it
cards.body: Go via literal 'Spanglish': it would have pleased me. Don't hunt for English 'liked'; just make the form that follows haber (-ado / -ido).

cards.title: debería = should
cards.body: 'Would owe' = should. In Spanish the next verb is always the 'to' form (English drops 'to' after should / can / must).

examples.en: You should come to my house to eat.
examples.es: Deberías venir a mi casa a comer.

cards.title: hablarle vs hablar con él
cards.body: Le could be him, her or formal you; con él / con ella removes the ambiguity.

examples.en: We should speak to him / them.
They would give it to me.

practice.en: We would have been able to go.
They would have come to eat.
You (informal) should come to my house.
They would give it to me.
